tracks.title: Biology
tracks.blurb: A compressed, prerequisite-ordered undergraduate biology sequence, from molecules and cells through genetics, regulation, physiology, and evolution to modern sequencing and omics technologies.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 2: The Chemical Foundation of Life
OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 3: Biological Macromolecules
OpenStax Biology 2e, 3.4: Proteins

lessons.title: Atoms, Bonds, and Water
lessons.focus: Covalent vs non-covalent bonds (hydrogen bonds, ionic, hydrophobic effect, van der Waals) and why water's polarity makes weak interactions the currency of molecular recognition. Emphasize that most biology (TF-DNA binding, protein folding, membranes) runs on many weak, reversible bonds.

lessons.title: Energy, Equilibrium, and Free Energy in Cells
lessons.focus: Gibbs free energy, equilibrium constants, coupling of unfavorable reactions to ATP hydrolysis, and pH/buffers. Frame binding affinity (Kd) and occupancy curves so later lessons on TF binding and receptor signaling feel quantitative.

lessons.title: Carbohydrates and Lipids
lessons.focus: Monosaccharides to polysaccharides, glycosylation, fatty acids, phospholipids, and sterols. Explain why lipid amphipathicity spontaneously forms bilayers and where these molecules show up in metabolism and membrane biology.

lessons.title: Amino Acids and the Four Levels of Protein Structure
lessons.focus: Amino acid side-chain chemistry, peptide bonds, and primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary structure. Connect sequence-determines-structure to why protein language models and AlphaFold can work.

lessons.title: Protein Function: Enzymes, Allostery, and Modifications
lessons.focus: Enzyme catalysis and Michaelis-Menten kinetics, allosteric regulation, and post-translational modifications (phosphorylation, ubiquitination, acetylation, glycosylation). Note that mRNA abundance misses PTM-level regulation, a key caveat when reading transcriptomics as a proxy for protein activity.

lessons.title: Nucleic Acids: DNA and RNA Chemistry
lessons.focus: Nucleotide structure, base pairing, strand directionality (5' to 3'), RNA secondary structure, and the chemical differences between DNA and RNA. Tie base-pairing to how hybridization-based assays and sequencing primers work.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 14: DNA Structure and Function
Scitable: DNA Packaging: Nucleosomes and Chromatin
Scitable: Genome Packaging in Prokaryotes

lessons.title: The Double Helix and Chromosomes
lessons.focus: DNA double helix geometry, chromosomes, ploidy, karyotypes, and how ~2 m of DNA fits in a nucleus via nucleosomes and higher-order folding. Contrast prokaryotic circular chromosomes and plasmids.

lessons.title: Anatomy of the Human Genome
lessons.focus: Genes, exons/introns, UTRs, promoters, repeats and transposable elements, pseudogenes, and the large noncoding fraction. Give rough numbers (genome size, ~20k protein-coding genes, % coding) the learner should keep in mind.

lessons.title: Reference Genomes and Gene Annotation
lessons.focus: What a reference assembly is (GRCh38, T2T-CHM13), coordinates, GTF/GFF annotations, Ensembl vs RefSeq gene models, transcript isoforms, and gene ID headaches. Explain how annotation choices change RNA-seq gene counts.

lessons.title: Organelle Genomes and Genome Diversity Across Life
lessons.focus: Mitochondrial DNA (maternal inheritance, high copy number, heteroplasmy), and how genome size and gene content vary across bacteria, yeast, flies, mice, and humans. Mention why mitochondrial read fraction is a single-cell QC metric.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 14.5: DNA Replication in Eukaryotes
OpenStax Biology 2e, 14.6: DNA Repair
Scitable: Genetic Mutation
Scitable: Errors in DNA Replication

lessons.title: How DNA Is Copied
lessons.focus: Replication origins, helicase, primase, DNA polymerases, leading/lagging strands, Okazaki fragments, and telomeres/telomerase. Keep it mechanistic but brief; link polymerase chemistry to PCR and sequencing-by-synthesis.

lessons.title: Fidelity and DNA Repair Pathways
lessons.focus: Proofreading, mismatch repair, base and nucleotide excision repair, and double-strand break repair (NHEJ vs homologous recombination). Connect NHEJ/HDR to how CRISPR edits are resolved and to BRCA-deficient cancers.

lessons.title: Types of Mutations and Their Consequences
lessons.focus: SNVs (synonymous, missense, nonsense), indels and frameshifts, splice-site mutations, copy number variants, and structural variants; germline vs somatic. Explain how each can or cannot be detected from RNA-seq.

lessons.title: Recombination and Transposable Elements
lessons.focus: Homologous recombination in meiosis, crossing over, and transposons/retrotransposons as mutagens and regulatory raw material. Note multimapping reads from repeats as a practical quantification problem.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 15: Genes and Proteins
OpenStax Biology 2e, 15.4: RNA Processing in Eukaryotes
Scitable: RNA Transcription by RNA Polymerase
Scitable: RNA Splicing

lessons.title: The Central Dogma and RNA Polymerases
lessons.focus: Information flow DNA to RNA to protein, the three eukaryotic RNA polymerases and what each makes, and the transcription cycle (initiation, elongation, termination). Highlight promoter-proximal pausing as a regulatory step.

lessons.title: Promoters and the Transcription Initiation Machinery
lessons.focus: Core promoter elements, general transcription factors, Mediator, and the preinitiation complex. Set up the distinction between core promoter and distal enhancers used in the regulation units.

lessons.title: mRNA Capping, Polyadenylation, and Export
lessons.focus: 5' capping, 3' cleavage and poly(A) tailing, alternative polyadenylation, and nuclear export. Explain why poly(A) capture and 3'-end counting (e.g. 10x 3' kits) bias what transcripts you observe.

lessons.title: Splicing and Alternative Splicing
lessons.focus: Spliceosome mechanics, splice-site signals, alternative splicing modes, and isoform diversity. Discuss why short-read gene-level counts hide isoform switching and how intronic reads enable spliced/unspliced (RNA velocity) estimates.

lessons.title: RNA Stability, Decay, and the Noncoding RNA Zoo
lessons.focus: mRNA half-lives, nonsense-mediated decay, and major RNA classes (rRNA, tRNA, snRNA, miRNA, lncRNA, circRNA). Note that steady-state RNA levels reflect both synthesis and decay.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 15.5: Ribosomes and Protein Synthesis
Scitable: Translation: DNA to mRNA to Protein
OpenStax Biology 2e, 4.4: The Endomembrane System and Proteins

lessons.title: The Genetic Code and the Ribosome
lessons.focus: Codons, reading frames, tRNAs and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and the steps of translation. Mention codon usage and ORF calling as computational tasks.

lessons.title: Translational Control
lessons.focus: Regulation via initiation factors, uORFs, mTOR signaling, and miRNAs; why mRNA and protein levels correlate only moderately. Introduce ribosome profiling as a translation-level readout.

lessons.title: Protein Targeting and the Secretory Pathway
lessons.focus: Signal peptides, ER, Golgi, vesicle trafficking, membrane proteins, and secreted proteins. Connect to why plasma cells and secretory cell types have distinctive transcriptomes (ER/UPR genes).

lessons.title: Protein Folding Quality Control and Degradation
lessons.focus: Chaperones, the unfolded protein response, ubiquitin-proteasome system, and autophagy. Explain how protein turnover rates add another layer between transcript and function.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 4: Cell Structure
OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 5: Structure and Function of Plasma Membranes
OpenStax Biology 2e, 4.5: The Cytoskeleton

lessons.title: Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic Cells and Organelles
lessons.focus: Compartmentalization, the nucleus, mitochondria, ER, Golgi, lysosomes, peroxisomes, and their functions. Give a sense of scale (cell sizes, molecule counts per cell, mRNA copies per gene).

lessons.title: Membranes and Transport
lessons.focus: Bilayer structure, membrane proteins, diffusion, channels, transporters, pumps, and endocytosis. Link ion gradients to neuron excitability later.

lessons.title: The Cytoskeleton and Motors
lessons.focus: Actin, microtubules, intermediate filaments, motor proteins, and their roles in shape, migration, division, and transport. Mention cytoskeletal genes as common cell-state markers.

lessons.title: Cell Junctions, Adhesion, and the Extracellular Matrix
lessons.focus: Tight/adherens/gap junctions, desmosomes, integrins, cadherins, and ECM components. Connect to epithelial vs mesenchymal states and EMT signatures in tumor and development data.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 9: Cell Communication
OpenStax Biology 2e, 9.2: Propagation of the Signal
Single-cell best practices: Cell-cell communication

lessons.title: Principles of Cell Signaling
lessons.focus: Ligands, receptors, signal amplification, feedback, and signal termination; autocrine, paracrine, endocrine, and juxtacrine modes. Frame signaling as information processing with dose-response and adaptation.

lessons.title: Receptor Classes: GPCRs, RTKs, Ion Channels, Nuclear Receptors
lessons.focus: How each receptor family transduces a signal, with canonical examples. Note which are major drug targets.

lessons.title: Intracellular Cascades: MAPK, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, Second Messengers
lessons.focus: Kinase cascades, scaffolds, second messengers (cAMP, Ca2+), and crosstalk. Emphasize that pathway activity is often post-translational and inferred indirectly from target-gene signatures (e.g. PROGENy-style footprints).

lessons.title: Developmental Signaling Pathways
lessons.focus: Wnt, Notch, Hedgehog, TGF-beta/BMP, JAK-STAT, and NF-kB: logic, key components, and transcriptional outputs. These recur in development, immunity, and cancer.

lessons.title: Cell-Cell Communication Inference from Expression Data
lessons.focus: How ligand-receptor databases and tools (CellPhoneDB, CellChat, LIANA) infer communication from scRNA-seq or spatial data, and their main assumptions and failure modes.

units.title: Cell Cycle, Division, and Cell Death

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 10: Cell Reproduction
OpenStax Biology 2e, 10.3: Control of the Cell Cycle
OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 11: Meiosis and Sexual Reproduction

lessons.title: Cell Cycle Phases and Mitosis
lessons.focus: G1/S/G2/M, chromosome condensation, spindle, and cytokinesis. Explain why cell-cycle genes dominate variation in proliferating single-cell data and how cell-cycle scoring/regression works.

lessons.title: Cyclins, CDKs, and Checkpoints
lessons.focus: CDK-cyclin oscillator, Rb-E2F switch, p53 and DNA damage checkpoints, spindle assembly checkpoint. Set up oncogenes and tumor suppressors.

lessons.title: Meiosis and Sexual Reproduction
lessons.focus: Homolog pairing, crossover, independent assortment, and nondisjunction. Connect to inheritance patterns and aneuploidy.

lessons.title: Apoptosis, Senescence, and Other Fates
lessons.focus: Intrinsic vs extrinsic apoptosis, caspases, necroptosis, senescence and SASP, quiescence. Note stress/dissociation signatures that can look like biology in scRNA-seq.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 12: Mendel's Experiments and Heredity
OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 13: Modern Understandings of Inheritance
Online Open Genetics (Nickle and Barrette-Ng), LibreTexts
Scitable: Gregor Mendel and Single-Gene Disorders

lessons.title: Mendel's Laws and Probability in Inheritance
lessons.focus: Segregation, independent assortment, Punnett squares, and pedigree reasoning, framed as probability the learner already knows.

lessons.title: Beyond Simple Dominance
lessons.focus: Incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, epistasis, penetrance, expressivity, and pleiotropy. Show how genotype-to-phenotype maps become nonlinear.

lessons.title: Linkage, Recombination, and Genetic Maps
lessons.focus: Linked genes, recombination frequency, centimorgans, and the idea of haplotypes. Sets up linkage disequilibrium and GWAS fine-mapping.

lessons.title: Sex Chromosomes, Dosage, and Chromosomal Abnormalities
lessons.focus: X/Y inheritance, dosage compensation (preview of X inactivation), aneuploidy, translocations, and their disease consequences. Mention sex as a covariate in expression analyses.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 19.1: Population Evolution
NHGRI: Genome-Wide Association Studies Fact Sheet
EMBL-EBI Training: Human genetic variation

lessons.title: Allele Frequencies and Hardy-Weinberg
lessons.focus: Population allele frequencies, Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, and what deviations indicate. Introduce population structure as a confounder.

lessons.title: Human Genetic Variation and Linkage Disequilibrium
lessons.focus: Common vs rare variants, haplotype blocks, LD, ancestry, and resources like gnomAD and 1000 Genomes.

lessons.title: Heritability and Complex Traits
lessons.focus: Polygenic architecture, heritability (and its misinterpretations), twin studies, and polygenic scores.

lessons.title: GWAS and Fine-Mapping
lessons.focus: GWAS design, multiple testing, Manhattan plots, LD-driven ambiguity, and fine-mapping. Emphasize that most hits are noncoding and regulatory.

lessons.title: eQTLs and Linking Variants to Function
lessons.focus: Expression and chromatin QTLs, colocalization, single-cell eQTLs, and how regulatory genomics data is used to interpret GWAS loci.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 16: Gene Expression
Working with Molecular Genetics (Hardison), LibreTexts
Single-cell best practices: Gene regulatory networks

lessons.title: Prokaryotic Gene Regulation: The Operon Logic
lessons.focus: lac and trp operons, repressors, activators, and inducers as the simplest model of regulatory logic. Use it to introduce cis vs trans.

lessons.title: Cis-Regulatory Elements: Promoters, Enhancers, Silencers, Insulators
lessons.focus: How distal enhancers act over long distances, enhancer grammar, and how these elements are annotated (ENCODE cCREs). Connect to ATAC peaks and enhancer-gene linking.

lessons.title: Transcription Factors and Binding Motifs
lessons.focus: TF families and DNA-binding domains, position weight matrices, motif databases (JASPAR), and why most motif matches are not bound. Link to motif enrichment in ATAC/ChIP analysis.

lessons.title: Combinatorial Control and Gene Regulatory Networks
lessons.focus: Cooperative binding, network motifs (feed-forward loops, feedback, bistability), master regulators, and cell identity. Discuss GRN inference from expression (SCENIC-style) and its limits.

lessons.title: The 3D Genome
lessons.focus: Chromatin loops, TADs, compartments, cohesin/CTCF loop extrusion, and Hi-C. Explain why enhancer-gene assignment by nearest gene is often wrong.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 16.3: Eukaryotic Epigenetic Gene Regulation
Scitable: Chromatin Remodeling in Eukaryotes
Scitable: The Role of Methylation in Gene Expression
NHGRI: Epigenomics Fact Sheet

lessons.title: Histone Modifications and the Histone Code
lessons.focus: Key marks (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K4me1, H3K27me3, H3K9me3, H3K36me3), writers/readers/erasers, and what each mark indicates about promoters, enhancers, and silenced regions.

lessons.title: DNA Methylation and Imprinting
lessons.focus: CpG islands, DNMTs and TETs, methylation in gene silencing, genomic imprinting, and methylation clocks. Mention bisulfite sequencing and methylation arrays.

lessons.title: Chromatin Accessibility and Remodeling
lessons.focus: Nucleosome positioning, pioneer factors, SWI/SNF remodelers, and how accessibility marks regulatory potential. Directly motivates ATAC-seq.

lessons.title: Epigenetic Memory: Polycomb, Trithorax, and X Inactivation
lessons.focus: How repressive and active states are maintained through cell divisions; X-chromosome inactivation by XIST. Note XIST as a sex marker in expression data.

lessons.title: Post-Transcriptional Regulation: miRNAs, lncRNAs, RBPs, RNA Modifications
lessons.focus: miRNA targeting, lncRNA mechanisms, RNA-binding proteins, and m6A. Explain why these layers add noise to RNA-to-protein inference.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 43: Animal Reproduction and Development
OpenStax Biology 2e, 43.7: Organogenesis and Vertebrate Axis Formation
Scitable: Gene Expression Regulates Cell Differentiation
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 3.6: Cellular Differentiation

lessons.title: From Zygote to Gastrula
lessons.focus: Fertilization, cleavage, blastocyst, gastrulation, and the three germ layers with what each becomes.

lessons.title: Morphogens, Patterning, and Hox Genes
lessons.focus: Morphogen gradients, positional information, body axes, Hox codes, and evolutionary conservation of developmental toolkits.

lessons.title: Differentiation and the Waddington Landscape
lessons.focus: Commitment, lineage restriction, bifurcations, and cell fate as attractor states. Connect to trajectory inference and pseudotime as computational analogs.

lessons.title: Stem Cells: Embryonic, Adult, and Induced Pluripotent
lessons.focus: Potency hierarchy, niches, hematopoietic hierarchy as a canonical example, Yamanaka reprogramming, and directed differentiation.

lessons.title: Organoids, Lineage Tracing, and Developmental Atlases
lessons.focus: Organoids as models, genetic and barcode-based lineage tracing, and single-cell developmental atlases. Discuss what clonal information adds beyond snapshot transcriptomes.

resources.title: OpenStax Microbiology, Ch. 17: Innate Nonspecific Host Defenses
OpenStax Microbiology, Ch. 18: Adaptive Specific Host Defenses
OpenStax Biology 2e, 42.2: Adaptive Immune Response
Single-cell best practices: Immune receptor profiling

lessons.title: Innate Immunity
lessons.focus: Barriers, pattern recognition receptors, macrophages, neutrophils, dendritic cells, NK cells, complement, and inflammation. Give the major marker genes for each cell type.

lessons.title: Antigen Presentation and MHC
lessons.focus: MHC class I vs II, antigen processing, HLA diversity, and how dendritic cells bridge innate and adaptive immunity.

lessons.title: T Cells: Development, Subsets, and Activation
lessons.focus: Thymic selection, CD4 helper subsets, CD8 cytotoxic cells, Tregs, activation signals, and exhaustion. Emphasize T-cell states as a heavily studied scRNA-seq problem.

lessons.title: B Cells and Antibodies
lessons.focus: B-cell activation, germinal centers, class switching, somatic hypermutation, plasma cells, and antibody structure.

lessons.title: V(D)J Recombination and Immune Repertoires
lessons.focus: How TCR/BCR diversity is generated, clonotypes, and how single-cell VDJ sequencing pairs receptor sequence with transcriptome.

lessons.title: Cytokines, Memory, and Immune Dysregulation
lessons.focus: Cytokine networks, immunological memory, vaccination, autoimmunity, and immunodeficiency. Mention interferon signatures as a common transcriptomic readout.

resources.title: NCI: What Is Cancer?
OpenStax Biology 2e, 10.4: Cancer and the Cell Cycle
OpenStax Biology 2e, 16.7: Cancer and Gene Regulation

lessons.title: Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
lessons.focus: Gain- vs loss-of-function, two-hit hypothesis, canonical genes (RAS, MYC, TP53, RB1, PTEN), and driver vs passenger mutations.

lessons.title: Hallmarks of Cancer
lessons.focus: The hallmark framework (sustained proliferation, evading suppressors and death, immortality, angiogenesis, invasion, metabolism, immune evasion, plus enabling characteristics) as a map for interpreting cancer omics.

lessons.title: Genomic Instability and Mutational Signatures
lessons.focus: Sources of mutations, mutational signatures, copy-number alterations, and inferring CNVs from scRNA-seq (inferCNV-style) to separate malignant from normal cells.

lessons.title: Clonal Evolution and Tumor Heterogeneity
lessons.focus: Tumor phylogenies, subclones, cancer stem cell ideas, plasticity, and therapy resistance.

lessons.title: The Tumor Microenvironment and Immuno-Oncology
lessons.focus: Cancer-associated fibroblasts, tumor-infiltrating immune cells, immune checkpoints, and immunotherapy response. Link to spatial and single-cell TME atlases.

lessons.title: Cancer Genomics Resources
lessons.focus: TCGA, ICGC, cell line resources (DepMap/CCLE), molecular subtyping, and common pitfalls such as purity confounding in bulk data.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 35: The Nervous System
OpenStax Biology 2e, 35.2: How Neurons Communicate
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, Ch. 12: The Nervous System and Nervous Tissue

lessons.title: Tissues and Organ Systems at a Glance
lessons.focus: The four tissue types, major organ systems, and how cell atlases (Human Cell Atlas, Tabula Sapiens) organize cell types by tissue.

lessons.title: Neurons and the Action Potential
lessons.focus: Resting potential, ion channels, action potential propagation, and myelination, using membrane transport knowledge.

lessons.title: Synapses and Neurotransmitters
lessons.focus: Chemical synapses, major neurotransmitter systems, receptors, and plasticity. Note neurotransmitter genes as neuron subtype markers.

lessons.title: Brain Cell Types and Neural Omics
lessons.focus: Neuronal classes, glia (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia), single-nucleus RNA-seq for brain, and cell-type taxonomies from large brain atlases.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 6: Metabolism
OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 7: Cellular Respiration
OpenStax Biology 2e, 7.6: Connections of Metabolic Pathways
Fundamentals of Biochemistry (Jakubowski and Flatt), LibreTexts

lessons.title: Energy Currency and Metabolic Logic
lessons.focus: ATP, NADH/NADPH, catabolism vs anabolism, and pathway regulation at committed steps.

lessons.title: Glycolysis and the TCA Cycle
lessons.focus: The flow of carbon from glucose to pyruvate to acetyl-CoA and through the TCA cycle, with key regulated enzymes.

lessons.title: Oxidative Phosphorylation and Mitochondria
lessons.focus: Electron transport chain, chemiosmosis, mitochondrial function beyond ATP, and mitochondrial gene signatures.

lessons.title: Lipid, Amino Acid, and Nucleotide Metabolism
lessons.focus: Fatty acid synthesis and oxidation, amino acid metabolism, nucleotide synthesis, and how pathways interconnect.

lessons.title: Metabolic Regulation, Cancer Metabolism, and Metabolomics
lessons.focus: mTOR/AMPK nutrient sensing, the Warburg effect, immunometabolism, and how metabolomics and expression-based flux inference work.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 18: Evolution and the Origin of Species
OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 19: The Evolution of Populations
OpenStax Biology 2e, Ch. 20: Phylogenies and the History of Life
Computational Biology: Genomes, Networks, and Evolution (Kellis et al.), LibreTexts

lessons.title: Natural Selection, Drift, and Speciation
lessons.focus: Mechanisms of evolutionary change, fitness, genetic drift, gene flow, and speciation.

lessons.title: Molecular Evolution and the Neutral Theory
lessons.focus: Substitution rates, dN/dS, purifying and positive selection, and molecular clocks.

lessons.title: Phylogenetics
lessons.focus: Tree concepts, homology, alignment-based tree building, and how evolutionary trees relate to cell lineage trees.

lessons.title: Gene Families, Orthology, and Model Organisms
lessons.focus: Gene duplication, paralogs vs orthologs, cross-species gene mapping, and the strengths and limits of mouse and other models for human biology.

lessons.title: Conservation as a Signal of Function
lessons.focus: Comparative genomics, conservation scores (phyloP, PhastCons), and how evolutionary information powers variant-effect predictors and protein language models.

resources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, 17.1: Biotechnology
NHGRI: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) Fact Sheet
NHGRI: What is genome editing?
NHGRI: DNA Sequencing Fact Sheet

lessons.title: PCR, Cloning, and Reporter Assays
lessons.focus: PCR and qPCR, reverse transcription, plasmids, cloning, and reporter assays (including massively parallel reporter assays). Explain PCR duplicates and UMIs.

lessons.title: Protein and Cell Assays: Antibodies, Westerns, Flow Cytometry, Imaging
lessons.focus: Antibody-based detection, western blots, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry and FACS, and fluorescence microscopy basics. Relate gating in flow cytometry to clustering.

lessons.title: Model Systems: Cell Lines, Primary Cells, Animals
lessons.focus: Immortalized lines, primary cells, iPSC-derived cells, mouse models, and experimental design concepts (replicates, controls, batch).

lessons.title: CRISPR and Genome Engineering
lessons.focus: Cas9 mechanism, guide design, knockouts, CRISPRi/CRISPRa, base and prime editing, and pooled screens.

lessons.title: Short-Read Sequencing: Illumina Chemistry
lessons.focus: Library prep, adapters, cluster amplification, sequencing-by-synthesis, paired-end reads, quality scores, FASTQ, and common artifacts.

lessons.title: Long-Read Sequencing: PacBio and Nanopore
lessons.focus: How each technology works, error profiles, and applications to full-length isoforms, structural variants, and direct methylation detection.

resources.title: Bioconductor RNA-seq workflow (rnaseqGene)
Analyzing RNA-seq data with DESeq2 (vignette)
EMBL-EBI Training: Functional genomics II
EMBL-EBI Training: Proteomics

lessons.title: Genome Sequencing and Variant Calling
lessons.focus: Alignment, duplicate marking, germline vs somatic calling, VCFs, and common filters. Brief, to give context for multiomics with genotypes.

lessons.title: Bulk RNA-seq: Design, Quantification, and Normalization
lessons.focus: Library types (poly(A) vs ribo-depletion, stranded), alignment vs pseudoalignment, count matrices, library-size and composition normalization, and replicate design.

lessons.title: Differential Expression Statistics
lessons.focus: Negative binomial GLMs, dispersion shrinkage, design matrices, multiple testing, and enrichment analysis. Emphasize why biological replicates matter.

lessons.title: Mapping the Epigenome: ChIP-seq, CUT&Tag, ATAC-seq, Bisulfite-seq
lessons.focus: Principles of each assay, peak calling, and what signal each captures.

lessons.title: Mass-Spectrometry Proteomics and Metabolomics
lessons.focus: Bottom-up proteomics, DDA vs DIA, quantification, missing values, phosphoproteomics, and how metabolomics differs.

lessons.title: Bulk Deconvolution and Integrating Bulk with Single-Cell
lessons.focus: Estimating cell-type proportions from bulk data using single-cell references and the assumptions involved.

resources.title: Single-cell best practices: Single-cell RNA sequencing
Single-cell best practices: Quality Control
Single-cell best practices: Data integration
Single-cell best practices: RNA velocity

lessons.title: scRNA-seq Technologies
lessons.focus: Plate-based vs droplet vs combinatorial indexing, cell barcodes and UMIs, 3' vs full-length chemistries, single-nucleus RNA-seq, and throughput/sensitivity trade-offs.

lessons.title: From Reads to Count Matrices and Quality Control
lessons.focus: Barcode processing, ambient RNA, doublets, QC metrics (counts, genes, mitochondrial fraction), and their biological confounds.

lessons.title: Normalization, Feature Selection, and Dimensionality Reduction
lessons.focus: Size factors, variance stabilization, highly variable genes, PCA, kNN graphs, UMAP/t-SNE caveats, and the sparsity/count nature of the data.

lessons.title: Clustering, Annotation, and Integration
lessons.focus: Graph-based clustering, marker-based and reference-based annotation, batch effects, and integration approaches.

lessons.title: Trajectories, Pseudotime, and RNA Velocity
lessons.focus: Pseudotemporal ordering, branch inference, spliced/unspliced dynamics, and the strong assumptions behind velocity.

lessons.title: Differential Expression and Composition Across Conditions
lessons.focus: Pseudobulk vs cell-level tests, pseudoreplication, and compositional analysis of cell-type proportions.

resources.title: Single-cell best practices: Single-cell ATAC sequencing
Single-cell best practices: Single-cell data resolved in space
Single-cell best practices: Perturbation modeling
Replogle et al., Genome-scale Perturb-seq (bioRxiv)

lessons.title: Single-Cell ATAC-seq and Multiome
lessons.focus: Tn5 tagmentation at single-cell resolution, peak vs bin features, gene activity scores, motif deviation (chromVAR), and joint RNA+ATAC assays.

lessons.title: CITE-seq and Multimodal Single-Cell Assays
lessons.focus: Antibody-derived tags for surface proteins, background/isotype issues, and other modalities (VDJ, lineage barcodes) measured alongside RNA.

lessons.title: Spatial Transcriptomics: Sequencing-Based Methods
lessons.focus: Spot-based capture (Visium), higher-resolution arrays, spot deconvolution, and spatially variable genes.

lessons.title: Spatial Transcriptomics: Imaging-Based Methods and Spatial Proteomics
lessons.focus: smFISH-derived methods (MERFISH, Xenium, CosMx), multiplexed protein imaging, cell segmentation, and neighborhood analysis.

lessons.title: Pooled CRISPR Screens and Perturb-seq
lessons.focus: Fitness screens vs single-cell readouts, guide assignment, MOI, perturbation efficiency, and what genome-scale Perturb-seq revealed.

lessons.title: Integrating Omics Layers: Principles and Pitfalls
lessons.focus: Paired vs unpaired integration, linking peaks to genes, and how the molecular layers learned in this track (chromatin, RNA, protein) relate, causally and statistically.

tracks.title: Advanced AI/ML
tracks.blurb: Research-level machine learning, from optimization and generalization theory through modern architectures, generative models, causality, and interpretability to biological foundation models.

resources.title: Dive into Deep Learning, Ch. 12: Optimization Algorithms
Cohen et al., Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability
Yang et al., Tensor Programs V: Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer (muP)

lessons.title: Loss Landscapes of Overparameterized Networks
lessons.focus: Nonconvexity, saddles vs local minima, mode connectivity, and why overparameterization makes optimization easier rather than harder.

lessons.title: SGD Noise and Implicit Regularization
lessons.focus: SGD as noisy gradient flow, the batch-size/learning-rate ratio, implicit bias toward low-norm or flat solutions, and what this means for small biological datasets.

lessons.title: Adaptive Optimizers and Schedules
lessons.focus: Adam/AdamW derivation, decoupled weight decay, warmup, cosine and WSD schedules, and why Adam dominates transformer training.

lessons.title: Initialization, Normalization, and Signal Propagation
lessons.focus: Variance-preserving initialization, LayerNorm vs BatchNorm vs RMSNorm, pre-norm vs post-norm, and muP for transferring hyperparameters across widths.

lessons.title: Sharpness and the Edge of Stability
lessons.focus: Hessian sharpness, progressive sharpening, edge-of-stability dynamics, and sharpness-aware minimization; what empirical evidence supports flat-minima arguments.

resources.title: Zhang et al., Understanding Deep Learning Requires Rethinking Generalization
Nakkiran et al., Deep Double Descent
Jacot et al., Neural Tangent Kernel
